geometry_edits.rationale: Expand the carved court so the ground void becomes more legible and usable as public space.
Turn the courtyard opening toward the verified access side to strengthen the frontage response.
Reduce the rotated offset so the intersected mass reads as a more continuous and coherent neighborhood figure.
Shift the roof/section toward a folded profile to better support a calm, inhabited neighborhood section.
Keep the long-span logic aligned with the existing dominant axis of the massing.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the primary mass by making the courtyard operation more decisive as the organizing urban void for neighborhood living.
Increase the void size enough to read as usable public space and a clearer ground threshold.
Align the open side to the site access side in program frame so the courtyard becomes an access-facing public figure.
Lower the terrace link so the bridge reads as a grounded public seam rather than a detached upper appendage.

rationale: The candidate is readable in multiple views as a compact courtyard-and-bridge mass, but the dominant form is still split between a low slab and a vertical central lump, so hierarchy is only moderate. The parcel response is weakly coherent: the mass sits inside the green boundary, but it behaves like a generic centered object more than a site-tuned edge figure. The thick blue frontage is not convincingly answered; the ground condition looks mostly sealed, with only a partial seam/void and no clearly legible public entry court aligned to access. In section, the object does not yet convincingly support neighborhood living as an active street building with a calm upper mass and public threshold. It is not a hard typology failure, but it is below program-fit because the frontage and ground logic are underdeveloped and the form leans too much toward a generic stacked/bridged object rather than an inhabited neighborhood threshold. References support a transferable courtyard/bridge/terrace principle, especially the central void and overhang language, but the candidate needs a clearer carved public void and a stronger access-side response.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More civic/cultural in tone than a compact neighborhood-living mass, but the courtyard-and-bridge logic is transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise ensemble with a clear central void and a bridge-like upper connection can support an active neighborhood edge without becoming a sealed box.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference reads as a larger campus/multi-block composition; candidate is much smaller and more singular.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, campus-like low-rise organization with a strong shared open space can inform a mixed neighborhood program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a more rectilinear civic object; candidate currently lacks the same clarity of the entry void.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A cut-out ground threshold with an overhanging upper mass is a strong model for active frontage and public void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more horizontal and porous; candidate is more tower-on-slab than perimeter atrium.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise massing with a central atrium and folded roof logic can support neighborhood commercial/living hybridity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more distributed and ramped; candidate compresses these ideas into a much tighter, less resolved form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Spread-out wings, courtyard-centered organization, and connecting bridges reinforce a legible public interior and active ground edge.

warnings: Visible massing is still somewhat generic and centered rather than strongly parcel-oriented.
Access-edge response is weak relative to the marked blue frontage.
The silhouette reads as a split slab-plus-upright rather than one dominant, continuous neighborhood gesture.
